data.reasoning: Both models reviewed the PKGBUILD and skwd-deck.install files and found them safe. The PKGBUILD is a standard -bin package downloading prebuilt binaries from the project's own GitHub releases with SHA-256 checksums. The install script performs standard systemd user service management during package removal. Report 1's inconclusive result was due to a tool error (HTTP 400) when reviewing .SRCINFO, not a security concern. .SRCINFO is a declarative metadata file with no executable code, so if the PKGBUILD is safe, .SRCINFO is inherently safe. Both models correctly identified no injection patterns, no dynamic code execution, and no suspicious network destinations.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool error in Report 1 (qwen3-235b) when attempting to review .SRCINFO, resulting in an HTTP 400 BadRequestError. This was not a security finding but an API failure. Report 2 (deepseek-v4-flash) successfully reviewed all files including .SRCINFO and found it safe. Since .SRCINFO contains no executable code and is auto-generated from PKGBUILD metadata, the tool error should not have resulted in an inconclusive verdict when the executable files (PKGBUILD and install script) were already confirmed safe.
coverage_issues: Report 1 failed to review .SRCINFO due to API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError), but this is a non-executable metadata file
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, timeouts) on non-executable files like .SRCINFO should not override successful reviews of executable files (PKGBUILD, install scripts) when determining final verdict
The audit tool should distinguish between 'could not review due to error' and 'found security issue' - a tool error is not a security finding
For -bin packages, prioritize review of PKGBUILD and install scripts as they contain the executable logic; .SRCINFO is declarative metadata and lower priority
